{{convert|19|°C|°F}}
35% [[humidity]]{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/uefaeuropaconferenceleague/2026/2047744_LU.pdf |title=Tactical Lineups – Final – Wednesday 27 May 2026 |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=27 May 2026 |access-date=27 May 2026}} | previous = [[2025 UEFA Conference League final|2025]] | next = ''[[2027 UEFA Conference League final|2027]]'' }} The '''2026 UEFA Conference League final''' was the final match of the [[2025–26 UEFA Conference League]], the fifth season of Europe's tertiary club [[association football|football]] tournament organised by [[UEFA]], and the second season since it was renamed from the UEFA Europa Conference League to the [[UEFA Conference League]]. It was played at the [[Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)|Red Bull Arena]] in [[Leipzig]], Germany, on 27 May 2026 between English club [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and Spanish club [[Rayo Vallecano]]. Crystal Palace won the match 1–0 for their first UEFA Conference League title.{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/news/02a5-20ba50a7a602-983af582dc90-1000/ |title=Crystal Palace 1–0 Rayo Vallecano: Jean-Philippe Mateta wins Conference League for the Eagles |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=27 May 2026 |access-date=27 May 2026}} As winners, they qualified for the league phase of the [[2026–27 UEFA Europa League]].{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/clypgp9wrp9t|title= Crystal Palace 1 Rayo Vallecano 0|date=27 May 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=28 May 2026}} ==Background== Crystal Palace, having [[Crystal Palace F.C. in European football|played in a major European competition]] for the first time, reached their first ever European final. They were aiming for their second major trophy, having won the [[FA Cup]] in [[2024–25 FA Cup|2025]], beating [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the final.{{cite news |date=17 May 2025 |title=Crystal Palace – 2024/25 FA Cup winners! |url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/announcement/crystal-palace-2024-25-fa-cup-champions/ |access-date=27 May 2026 |publisher=Crystal Palace F.C.}} As winners of the FA Cup, they were initially given a [[2025–26 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] league phase berth but due to [[Multi-club ownership (association football)|multi-club ownership]] restrictions regarding club stakeholder [[John Textor]] also having ownership of French team [[Olympique Lyonnais]] via [[Eagle Football Holdings]], Crystal Palace's European qualification berth was switched with [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]]'s, who initially took England's Conference League berth, by UEFA to prevent clubs with the same owners competing in the same tournament, as Lyon finished in a higher [[2024–25 Ligue 1|league position in France]] than Palace [[2024–25 Premier League|did in England]].{{cite web |title=The CFCB First Chamber renders decision on Crystal Palace and Olympique Lyonnais |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/029b-1e361573fefc-94aa466245fc-1000--the-cfcb-first-chamber-renders-decision-on-crystal-palace-an/ |website=[[UEFA]] |access-date=11 July 2025}}{{Cite web |date=2025-07-11 |title=Crystal Palace set to be replaced by Nottingham Forest in Europa League |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ckg5260zzp2o |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}} Rayo Vallecano also reached their first ever European final, and were aiming for a first major title. Rayo Vallecano had previously qualified for the quarter-finals of the [[2000–01 UEFA Cup#Quarter-finals|2000–01 UEFA Cup]], losing 4–2 on aggregate to fellow Spanish side [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].{{cite web |title=Alavés vs. Rayo Vallecano Match Report – Thursday March 8, 2001 (Leg 1) |url=https://fbref.com/en/matches/ff6ffb94/Alaves-Rayo-Vallecano-March-8-2001-UEFA-Cup |access-date=27 May 2026 |website=FBref}} ==Venue== [[File:Leipzig stadium.jpg|thumb|[[Red Bull Arena (Leipzig)|Red Bull Arena]] in [[Leipzig]] hosted the final.]] ===Host selection=== On 17 May 2023, UEFA opened the bidding process for the final, which was held in parallel with that of the [[2027 UEFA Conference League final|2027 final]]. Interested bidders could bid for either one or both of the finals. Additionally, bidding associations could only be appointed one UEFA final in a given year. The proposed venues had to include natural grass and be ranked as a [[UEFA stadium categories|UEFA category four stadium]], with a gross capacity of 30,000 to 60,000 preferred. Vallecano|1–0]] (A) |} ==Match== ===Summary=== Just before half-time, Crystal Palace's [[Tyrick Mitchell]] missed the target with a diving header from close range after a pass from [[Adam Wharton]]. Crystal Palace went in front in the 51st minute, an Adam Wharton shot from outside the penalty area on the left was saved by Rayo Vallecano goalkeeper [[Augusto Batalla]] but the rebound went straight to [[Jean-Philippe Mateta]] who diverted the ball with his left leg to the net from six yards out. [[Yeremy Pino]] almost made it 2–0 when his free-kick hit both posts and stayed out.{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/27/crystal-palace-rayo-vallecano-conference-league-final-match-report|title= Crystal Palace win Conference League after Mateta strike sinks Rayo Vallecano|date=27 May 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=28 May 2026}} Jean-Philippe Mateta also had a low shot saved by Augusto Batalla soon after. Crystal Palace held on to win the game 1–0 and claim a first European trophy.{{cite web|url= https://www.skysports.com/football/crystal-palace-vs-rayo-vallecano/report/554966|title= Crystal Palace 1-0
